answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, with the stake slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Like tending one orchard rather than claiming every mesa and dune on the map, one honest identity earns reputation only through verified completed work over time, so an attacker must pay a fresh stake and wait out a fresh history for every fake, while a single real agent keeps its standing at no extra cost.
